nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 7:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Gather from MySQL
nodes.notes: Selects rows from the MySQL table (returnAll) — the read side of the store. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Gather from Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Email Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Blend Sources
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Roll Up KPIs
nodes.notes: Group-by + aggregate (like a pivot table) — turns raw rows into KPI numbers.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency

nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Send a weekly summary: MySQL, scheduled

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers newsletters work end to end across MySQL, Google Sheets, Discord and Slack.

It moves through 21 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Gather from MySQL
3. Gather API Numbers
4. Gather from Google Sheets
5. Blend Sources
6. Roll Up KPIs
7. Write Executive Summary (AI)
8. Groq Chat Model
9. Compose HTML Report
10. Send Report via Discord
11. Enrich with Reference Data
12. Fold In Enrichment Fields
13. Stamp Completion Time
14. Persist Run Metadata
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
18. Archive Row Snapshot
19. Summarize Run Stats
20. Append Audit Row (MySQL)
21. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Gather from MySQL → Gather API Numbers → Gather from Google Sheets → Blend Sources → Roll Up KPIs → Write Executive Summary (AI) → Groq Chat Model → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Discord → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (MySQL) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping MySQL and Google Sheets aligned by hand for newsletters
- Newsletters work where "Gather from MySQL" is still a manual step before MySQL
- Newsletters work that only reaches MySQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps MySQL and Google Sheets in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in MySQL or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 24 nodes of this newsletters build
- A failed MySQL or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 24 nodes in this newsletters build
- Every newsletters run leaves an audit row behind, alongside MySQL
- The newsletters AI step is isolated from MySQL, so models swap without touching the other 24 nodes

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2 / service account; Groq API key; MySQL connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
